title: Network operator clauses and observable proof playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working playbook for the Private product: it defines minimum operator contract clauses, the observable "proof" (audit events and artifacts) we require from customer-managed networking handoffs, and a lightweight approval-gate matrix that ties legal/operator commitments to technical telemetry. Goal is to reduce ambiguous signoffs, accelerate onboards, and provide SRE/Support with deterministic signals when to accept/deny/roll back customer edge changes.

Background / problem statement:
- Customers run customer-managed VPCs, VPNs, or on-prem appliances that interface with Redwood Private. Current handoff paperwork is inconsistent: tickets, emails, and ad-hoc Slack approvals are common.
- When incidents happen (routing changes, peering TTLs, firewall rules), support and engineering spend hours piecing together what changed and when. Audit trails are often missing or incomplete.
- Legal and security teams want explicit operator clauses for: (1) how long customer must retain network logs, (2) evidence required for attestation, (3) acceptable SLA windows for rollback.

Scope:
- Includes: operator contract language templates, required audit event set (what to capture), approval-gate definitions for onboarding and post-onboard network changes, sample log retention policies, and an operations checklist for day-0/1 handoffs.
- Excludes: deep PKI/KMS key exchange specs (refer to control-plane-ops PRD), per-customer legal negotiations, and private connectivity billing.

Stakeholders:
- Product: Leah Morrison (owner), Priya Desai
- Solutions Eng / Onboarding: Rafael Gomez, Benji Wu
- Security & Compliance: TBD (security reviewer)
- Legal: Contract owner for template clauses
- SRE / Support: rotation leads who will enforce gate checks during incidents

Definitions / terminology (short):
- Proof artifact: any immutable record we accept as evidence (signed syslog export, SIEM event id, packet capture hash, timestamped approval email with message-id).
- Approval gate: a named step in onboarding/change flow that must be satisfied before progressing (e.g., "Edge ACL signoff").
- Operator clause: contract language the customer agrees to that binds them to retention/attestation behavior.

High-level goals (what success looks like):
- Reduce time-to-resolution for suspected customer-network incidents by 40% via reliable audit signals.
- Make 90% of network onboards go live without >1 follow-up ask for supplemental logs.
- Provide legal-approved minimal retention and attestation language that fits enterprise buyers.

User stories / examples:
- As an SRE I want a single canonical event id that proves the customer's firewall rule change at 2025-01-10T17:21:43Z so I can correlate it with our access logs and determine cause.
- As a solutions engineer I want a checklist I can give the customer prior to handover so the first live test doesn't get blocked by missing flow logs.
- As Legal I want customers to agree to retain flow logs for at least 90 days and to permit short-term forensic exports on request.

Functional requirements (draft):
1) Operator clause template (customer-facing) - must include:
   - Agreed log types (flow logs/syslog/conntrack) and retention period (default 90 days).
   - Export mechanism: customer agrees to produce a signed log bundle (GPG-signed tar.gz or cloud-provider signed export) within 48 hours of request.
   - Change notification: customer will post network-change intent to a dedicated ticket channel 72 hours before disruptive changes; for emergency changes must notify within 2 hours.
   - Break-glass rollback cooperation: customer agrees to allow Redwood to request rollback and to provide logs to validate rollback.

2) Observable proof set (minimum):
   - Edge ACL events: timestamped add/remove with username and change-id
   - VPC Flow Logs / Netflow: 1-minute granularity preferred for first 7 days after major change, 5-minute thereafter
   - BGP peering session logs: session up/down and table deltas for 24 hours around change window
   - NAT / SNAT mappings: mapping snapshots at change time and 5-minute intervals for 30 minutes
   - Packet capture hash: optional but strongly recommended for validated incidents (pcap SHA256)

3) Audit log schema (example lines we accept) - these are examples of canonicalized events Redwood will ingest or accept as proof. Customer should provide logs in newline-delimited JSON where each record is an event.
   Example event: 
   {"ts":"2025-01-10T17:21:43Z","source":"customer-firewall-01.example.com","event_type":"acl_change","actor":"alice@example.com","change_id":"chg-20250110-8f3a","details":"allow tcp 443 from 10.2.0.0/16 to 172.18.0.0/24"} 

   Flow log sample (ndjson):
   {"ts":"2025-01-10T17:22:01Z","src_ip":"10.2.1.15","dst_ip":"34.120.10.55","src_port":443,"dst_port":56422,"proto":6,"bytes":1420,"log_type":"vpc_flow"} 

   BGP session event sample: 
   {"ts":"2025-01-10T17:20:01Z","event_type":"bgp_state_change","peer":"rtr-peer-east","old_state":"established","new_state":"idle","session_id":"bgp-88"} 

   NOTE: schema fields above are minimums; customers may supply provider-native formats (GCP/AWS) but must include a mapping document to these canonical fields during onboarding.

Non-functional requirements / constraints:
- All proof artifacts must be tamper-evident: signed exports or provider-signed snapshots preferred.
- Retention defaults: 90 days for flow logs, 365 days for change-event metadata (who changed what), 30 days for pcaps unless otherwise negotiated.
- Data transfer: logs must be exportable via HTTPS/SFTP or by creating a signed cloud-storage object with a time-limited signed URL.
- Privacy: customers can mask IPs in shared artifacts by using reversible tokenization; unmasking requires a data-access request and justification.

Approval-gate matrix (simple):
- Gate: Edge ACL signoff (pre-go-live) => Required proof: ACL change event + Flow logs for test window + signed ticket acceptance => Who approves: Solutions Eng + Customer Network Owner => Pass criteria: ACL event exists and test traffic succeeded; otherwise reject.
- Gate: BGP peering (pre-go-live) => Required proof: BGP session up, route table snapshot, eBGP MD5 config check => Who approves: Network Lead + SRE => Pass: session stable for 5min and routes present.
- Gate: Post-change emergency (post-live) => Required proof: Signed export of change_id + 1-hour flow log window + packet capture hash (if requested) => Who approves: Oncall SRE in regional rotation => Pass: evidence aligns with observed outage window.

Operator contract language (draft excerpt):
- "Customer will retain network flow logs and change-event metadata for a minimum of ninety (90) days following creation. Upon request from Redwood, Customer will make available, within forty-eight (48) hours, a tamper-evident export of those logs for forensic analysis. Customer further agrees to provide timely cooperation in rollback requests and to maintain a single, auditable channel for change notifications."

Onboarding / runbook (day-0 through day-3):
- Day -7: Solutions Eng shares checklist and canonical log schema mapping doc via PRD ticket.
- Day -3: Customer provides a sample 24-hour dataset exported to staging bucket (signed object). Engineering runs parser and validates mapping.
- Day -1: Dry-run change in staging; Solutions Eng verifies ACL events and flow visibility.
- Day 0: Production handoff — both parties run a short 30-minute smoke test with live traffic. Approvers sign Gate:Edge ACL signoff.
- Day 1-3: Post-onboard monitoring at higher fidelity: 1-min flow logs retained for 7 days; we monitor anomalies.

Operational play snippets (todo / copy-ready):
- Parser tool: we will provide a small reference script (Python) that validates ndjson fields and computes event hashes. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy/tree/main/tools/log-validator (stub PR exists).
- Quick attestation checklist for Support: 1) pull signed export, 2) verify signature, 3) map change_id to ticket, 4) surface matching flow log entries.

Acceptance criteria (minimal):
- Solutions Eng can validate a customer-provided sample dataset within 48 hours using the reference parser.
- At least one enterprise customer signs the operator clause in pilot and can produce a signed export within SLA.
- SRE-run incident where operator proof reduced diagnostic time vs historical incidents (measured in follow-up survey).

Metrics to track (during pilot):
- % of onboards that pass Gate:Edge ACL signoff without extra asks
- Mean time to diagnostic when incident suspected to be on customer network (target -40% reduction)
- % of evidence requests satisfied within 48 hours

Open questions / risks (working list):
- Legal: are the 48-hour and retention windows acceptable across EU customers (GDPR / DPA implications)? (ACTION: loop in Legal)
- For customers using third-party SD-WAN appliances, can we accept management-plane logs or do we need in-path flow captures?
- Cost: more frequent 1-min flows for first 7 days increases egress/storage cost; who bears it? (we should add a billing note).

Next steps / short-term plan:
- Get security and legal review on operator clause (target: two-week turnaround).
- Implement reference parser and add a Confluence page with examples (owner: Rafael).
- Pilot with 1-2 customers targeted for Q1 2025 (solutions eng owners: Priya & Benji).

Notes / ephemeral items (notes-to-self style):
- TODO: create a lightweight signed template for "signed export" (consider using AWS export with presigned URL + object metadata + SHA256).
- TODO: add one-pager for sales that summarizes obligations in plain language (one-page checklist).
- Slack anchor: threads are in #priv-deploy-ops (search "audit proof playbook").

References:
- see Confluence: CONFLUENCE-PRIVNET-88 (log schema mapping)
- jira: JIRA-PRIVNET-212 (onboard ticket template)
- github: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy/pull/342 (parser stub)

Revision history:

- 2024-12-02: added schema examples and gate matrix (Rafael)
